questions.question: Who is merchant of record in an ACP purchase made through ChatGPT?
questions.explanation: OpenAI's docs say the merchant is merchant of record and handles refunds and chargebacks.

questions.question: Which header is required on every ACP POST since version 2026-04-17?
questions.explanation: 2026-04-17 made Idempotency-Key mandatory on all POSTs; Signature, Timestamp and Request-Id are recommended.

questions.question: Which allowance reason does ACP define?
questions.explanation: one_time is the only defined reason.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a required Allowance field?
questions.explanation: The allowance requires reason, max_amount, currency, checkout_session_id, merchant_id and expires_at.

questions.question: How are ACP versions published?
options: Dated spec folders with no tags
questions.explanation: Versions are dated folders; the repository has no releases or tags.

questions.question: Which status signals that a merchant requires 3DS?
questions.explanation: The merchant sets authentication_required and must include authentication_metadata.

questions.question: What does the spec return when the same Idempotency-Key arrives with a different body?
questions.explanation: The spec uses 422 idempotency_conflict; OpenAI's docs say 409.

questions.question: How are ACP order webhooks authenticated?
questions.explanation: Merchants sign with HMAC-SHA256 over timestamp, a dot and the raw body.

questions.question: What did OpenAI announce on 2026-03-24?
options: Merchants can use their own checkout and ACP extends to product discovery
questions.explanation: OpenAI said the first Instant Checkout lacked flexibility and focused ACP on discovery.
